name: confirm
title: Confirm
description: Replaces the browser's confirm() with a styled dialog for forms, submit buttons and links that carry data-confirm.

attributes.name: data-confirm
attributes.description: The question to ask. Submitting the form or following the link waits for the answer. A data-confirm on the submit button wins over one on the form.

attributes.name: data-confirm-text
attributes.description: Optional explanation shown under the question.

attributes.name: data-confirm-dialog
attributes.description: The dialog used to ask. Put one on the page, usually in the layout. Its buttons must close it with value="confirm" or another value (cancel).

attributes.name: data-confirm-dialog-target="text"
attributes.description: Receives data-confirm-text, or the default text.

attributes.name: data-confirm-dialog-default-text
attributes.description: Text used when the trigger has no data-confirm-text. Defaults to "This action cannot be undone and may have permanent consequences."

notes: The dialog reports the answer through its returnValue: a <form method="dialog"> button with value="confirm" confirms; anything else, including Escape, cancels.
When no data-confirm-dialog is on the page, the browser's native confirm() is used.
After confirming, the original submission is replayed with form.requestSubmit(submitter) or link.click(), so other submit and click handlers still run.
This replaces css-zero's Turbo-specific turbo_confirm component.
